title: The Most Useful React Hooks
description: The most useful React hooks, useState and useEffect, explained with their parameters, examples and the key points on when to use each.

blocks.v: useState is a React Hook that allows you to add state to functional components. It enables you to manage dynamic values within your component, such as user inputs, toggles, counters, or any data that may change over time.

v: initialValue : The initial state value. It can be any data type (e.g., string, number, object, array, etc.).
setState : A function used to update the state value.
Re-renders : Updating the state via setState triggers a re-render of the component.
State is isolated : Each useState call creates its own state, even if used multiple times in the same component.
Lazy Initialisation : If initialValue requires computation, you can pass a function to useState :

blocks.v: useEffect is a React Hook that lets you perform side effects in functional components. It’s a replacement for lifecycle methods like componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate, and componentWillUnmount in class components.
It runs after the render is committed to the DOM and can be used for a variety of purposes such as fetching data, subscribing to events, or manipulating the DOM.

v: Effect Function ( () => {} ) : Contains the side-effect logic.
Dependency Array ( [dependencies] ) : Determines when the effect should re-run:

blocks.v: Empty array ( [] ) : Effect runs only once (on mount).

v: Array with dependencies : Effect runs when dependencies change.
No array : Effect runs after every render (not recommended unless necessary).
Side Effects : Ideal for tasks that don't directly affect rendering, like data fetching, setting up subscriptions, or manually modifying the DOM.
Cleanup Function : Always include cleanup logic if the effect involves subscriptions or asynchronous operations to prevent memory leaks.
Dependency Array : Properly specify dependencies to avoid unnecessary re-renders or stale values.
